monoidal category `C`.  The treatment is deliberately restricted to the results

periodicity.  In particular we do **not** treat braided tensor products, finite

* `HasPeriodAt X m d` : there is an isomorphism `mpow X m ≅ mpow X (m+d)`

* `IsPeriodic X` : `X` has some positive period.

* `isPeriodic_of_iso_lt` : a witness pair `m < n` with `mpow X m ≅ mpow X n`

import Mathlib

open CategoryTheory MonoidalCategory

namespace MonoidalPeriodicity

variable {C : Type*} [Category C] [MonoidalCategory C]

/-- The right-associated `n`-fold tensor power of `X`. -/
def mpow (X : C) : ℕ → C
  | 0 => 𝟙_ C
  | (n + 1) => X ⊗ mpow X n

@[simp]
theorem mpow_zero (X : C) : mpow X 0 = 𝟙_ C := rfl

@[simp]
theorem mpow_succ (X : C) (n : ℕ) : mpow X (n + 1) = X ⊗ mpow X n := rfl

/-- The first tensor power is isomorphic to `X` itself (via the right unitor). -/
def mpowOneIso (X : C) : mpow X 1 ≅ X := ρ_ X

/-- Index equalities induce isomorphisms of tensor powers. -/
def mpowCongr (X : C) {m n : ℕ} (h : m = n) : mpow X m ≅ mpow X n :=
  eqToIso (by rw [h])

/-- The additive comparison isomorphism for tensor powers:
`mpow X (m + n) ≅ mpow X m ⊗ mpow X n`.  Proved by induction on `m`, transporting
along the right unitor and the associator (right-associated recursion). -/
def mpow_add_iso (X : C) (m n : ℕ) : mpow X (m + n) ≅ mpow X m ⊗ mpow X n := by
  induction m with
  | zero => exact mpowCongr X (Nat.zero_add n) ≪≫ (λ_ (mpow X n)).symm
  | succ m ih =>
      exact mpowCongr X (Nat.succ_add m n) ≪≫ whiskerLeftIso X ih ≪≫
        (α_ X (mpow X m) (mpow X n)).symm

/-- A concrete periodicity witness "starting at `m`": an isomorphism
`mpow X m ≅ mpow X (m + d)`. -/
def HasPeriodAt (X : C) (m d : ℕ) : Prop := Nonempty (mpow X m ≅ mpow X (m + d))

/-- `X` has period `d` if `d` is positive and some witness `HasPeriodAt X m d` exists. -/
def HasPeriod (X : C) (d : ℕ) : Prop := 0 < d ∧ ∃ m, HasPeriodAt X m d

/-- `X` is periodic if it has some positive period. -/

    Requires `0 ≤ τ` for uniqueness of the winning class.
-/
lemma abstainClassifier_some_iff
    {X : Type*}
    (s : Fin 3 → X → ℝ) {τ : ℝ} (hτ : 0 ≤ τ) (x : X) (i : Fin 3) :
    abstainClassifier s τ x = some i ↔ τ < classMargin s i x := by
  constructor <;> intro h;
  · unfold abstainClassifier at h;
    split_ifs at h ; have := Classical.choose_spec ( by aesop : ∃ i, τ < classMargin s i x ) ; aesop;
  · -- Applying the definition of `abstainClassifier` from the hypothesis `h`.
    unfold abstainClassifier;
    split_ifs with h';
    · exact congr_arg _ ( classMargin_gt_tau_unique s hτ ( Classical.choose_spec h' ) h );
    · exact h' ⟨ i, h ⟩

/-
The abstain classifier returns `none` iff all class margins are at most `τ`.
-/
lemma abstainClassifier_none_iff
    {X : Type*}
    (s : Fin 3 → X → ℝ) (τ : ℝ) (x : X) :
    abstainClassifier s τ x = none ↔ ∀ i, classMargin s i x ≤ τ := by
  unfold abstainClassifier;
  split_ifs <;> simp_all +decide [ Classical.not_not ]

/-! ## Lipschitz bounds -/

/-
Class margin is `Kd`-Lipschitz under pairwise-difference Lipschitz scores.
-/
lemma classMargin_lipschitz
    {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
    {s : Fin 3 → X → ℝ} {Kd : ℝ}
    (hLip : PairwiseDiffLipschitz s Kd) :
    ∀ i : Fin 3, ∀ x y : X,
      |classMargin s i x - classMargin s i y| ≤ Kd * dist x y := by
  intro i x y;
  -- By definition of classMargin, we have that classMargin s i x is the infimum of s i x - s j x over all j ≠ i.
  have h_inf : ∀ x, classMargin s i x = s i x - (Finset.univ.erase i).sup' (erase_nonempty i) (fun j => s j x) := by
    intro; rfl;
  -- By definition of classMargin, we have that classMargin s i x is the infimum of s i x - s j x over all j ≠ i. Therefore, we can write:
  have h_inf_le : ∀ x y, classMargin s i x - classMargin s i y ≤ Kd * dist x y := by
    intro x y
    obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ : ∃ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, s j y = (Finset.univ.erase i).sup' (erase_nonempty i) (fun j => s j y) := by
      have := Finset.exists_max_image ( Finset.univ.erase i ) ( fun j => s j y ) ( erase_nonempty i );
      exact ⟨ this.choose, this.choose_spec.1, le_antisymm ( Finset.le_sup' ( fun j => s j y ) this.choose_spec.1 ) ( Finset.sup'_le _ _ fun j hj => this.choose_spec.2 j hj ) ⟩;
    have := hLip i j x y;
    linarith [ abs_le.mp this, h_inf x, h_inf y, show s j x ≤ ( Finset.univ.erase i ).sup' ( erase_nonempty i ) ( fun j => s j x ) from Finset.le_sup' ( fun j => s j x ) hj.1 ];
  exact abs_sub_le_iff.mpr ⟨ h_inf_le x y, by simpa [ dist_comm ] using h_inf_le y x ⟩

/-
Top margin is `Kd`-Lipschitz under pairwise-difference Lipschitz scores.
-/
lemma topMargin_lipschitz
    {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
    {s : Fin 3 → X → ℝ} {Kd : ℝ}
    (hLip : PairwiseDiffLipschitz s Kd) :
    ∀ x y : X, |topMargin s x - topMargin s y| ≤ Kd * dist x y := by
  intro x y; rw [ topMargin, topMargin ] ; simp +decide [ *, Fin.univ_succ ] ;
  -- Apply the Lipschitz property to each term in the maximum.
  have h_max_lip : ∀ i : Fin 3, |classMargin s i x - classMargin s i y| ≤ Kd * dist x y := by
    exact fun i => classMargin_lipschitz hLip i x y;
  refine' abs_sub_le_iff.mpr ⟨ _, _ ⟩ <;> cases max_cases ( classMargin s 0 x ) ( max ( classMargin s 1 x ) ( classMargin s 2 x ) ) <;> cases max_cases ( classMargin s 0 y ) ( max ( classMargin s 1 y ) ( classMargin s 2 y ) ) <;> cases max_cases ( classMargin s 1 x ) ( classMargin s 2 x ) <;> cases max_cases ( classMargin s 1 y ) ( classMargin s 2 y ) <;> linarith [ abs_le.mp ( h_max_lip 0 ), abs_le.mp ( h_max_lip 1 ), abs_le.mp ( h_max_lip 2 ) ]

/-! ## Core scalar threshold robustness -/

/-- A Lipschitz function that is above a threshold at `x` stays above at `y`
    if `y` is close enough. -/
lemma scalar_threshold_above
    {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
    {f : X → ℝ} {K τ : ℝ} {x y : X}
    (hLip : ∀ x y : X, |f x - f y| ≤ K * dist x y)
    (hK : 0 ≤ K)
    (_ : τ < f x)
    (hradius : dist x y < (f x - τ) / K) :
    τ < f y := by
  contrapose! hradius
  exact div_le_of_le_mul₀ (by positivity) (by positivity)
    (by linarith [abs_le.mp (hLip x y)])

/-- A Lipschitz function that is below a threshold at `x` stays below at `y`
    if `y` is close enough. -/
lemma scalar_threshold_below
    {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
    {f : X → ℝ} {K τ : ℝ} {x y : X}
    (hLip : ∀ x y : X, |f x - f y| ≤ K * dist x y)
    (hK : 0 ≤ K)
    (_ : f x < τ)
    (hradius : dist x y < (τ - f x) / K) :
    f y < τ := by
  contrapose! hradius
  exact div_le_of_le_mul₀ (by positivity) (by positivity)
    (by linarith [abs_le.mp (hLip x y)])

/-! ## Main robustness theorems -/

/-- **Sharp non-abstention robustness**: if class `i` has margin above `τ` at `x`,
    then it has margin above `τ` at any `y` within the certified radius. -/
theorem abstain_classifier_some_of_margin_ball
    {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
    {s : Fin 3 → X → ℝ} {Kd τ : ℝ} {x y : X} {i : Fin 3}
    (hLip : PairwiseDiffLipschitz s Kd)
    (hKd : 0 ≤ Kd)
    (hmargin : τ < classMargin s i x)
    (hradius : dist x y < (classMargin s i x - τ) / Kd) :
    τ < classMargin s i y :=
  scalar_threshold_above (classMargin_lipschitz hLip i) hKd hmargin hradius

/-- **Classifier-level preservation of `some i`**: the abstain classifier returns the
    same class at a nearby point. Requires `0 ≤ τ` for uniqueness. -/
theorem abstain_classifier_eq_some_preserved
    {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
    {s : Fin 3 → X → ℝ} {Kd τ : ℝ} {x y : X} {i : Fin 3}
    (hLip : PairwiseDiffLipschitz s Kd)
    (hKd : 0 < Kd)
    (hτ : 0 ≤ τ)
    (hx : abstainClassifier s τ x = some i)
    (hradius : dist x y < (classMargin s i x - τ) / Kd) :
    abstainClassifier s τ y = some i := by
  rw [abstainClassifier_some_iff _ hτ] at hx ⊢
  exact abstain_classifier_some_of_margin_ball hLip (le_of_lt hKd) hx hradius

/-
**Half-radius corollary for non-abstention preservation**.
-/
theorem abstain_classifier_eq_some_preserved_half_radius
    {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
    {s : Fin 3 → X → ℝ} {Kd τ : ℝ} {x y : X} {i : Fin 3}
    (hLip : PairwiseDiffLipschitz s Kd)
    (hKd : 0 < Kd)
    (hτ : 0 ≤ τ)
    (hmargin : τ < classMargin s i x)
    (hradius : dist x y < (classMargin s i x - τ) / (2 * Kd)) :
    abstainClassifier s τ y = some i := by
  exact abstain_classifier_eq_some_preserved hLip hKd hτ ( by simpa using abstainClassifier_some_iff s hτ x i |>.2 hmargin ) ( by rw [ lt_div_iff₀ ( by positivity ) ] at *; linarith )

/-
**Sharp abstention robustness**: if top margin is below `τ` at `x`,
    then the classifier abstains at any `y` within the certified radius.
-/
theorem abstain_classifier_none_of_topMargin_ball
    {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
    {s : Fin 3 → X → ℝ} {Kd τ : ℝ} {x y : X}
    (hLip : PairwiseDiffLipschitz s Kd)
    (hKd : 0 ≤ Kd)
    (hmargin : topMargin s x < τ)
    (hradius : dist x y < (τ - topMargin s x) / Kd) :
    abstainClassifier s τ y = none := by
  -- By the scalar_threshold_below lemma, since topMargin s x < τ and dist x y < (τ - topMargin s x) / Kd, we have topMargin s y < τ.
  have h_topMargin_y : topMargin s y < τ := by
    have := topMargin_lipschitz hLip x y;
    cases eq_or_lt_of_le hKd <;> simp_all +decide [ lt_div_iff₀ ];
    · subst_vars; linarith [ abs_le.mp this ] ;
    · linarith [ abs_le.mp this ];
  exact abstainClassifier_none_iff s τ y |>.2 fun i => le_trans ( Finset.le_sup' ( fun i => classMargin s i y ) ( Finset.mem_univ i ) ) h_topMargin_y.le

/-
**Half-radius corollary for abstention preservation**.
-/
theorem abstain_classifier_none_preserved_half_radius
    {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
    {s : Fin 3 → X → ℝ} {Kd τ : ℝ} {x y : X}
    (hLip : PairwiseDiffLipschitz s Kd)
    (hKd : 0 < Kd)
    (hmargin : topMargin s x < τ)
    (hradius : dist x y < (τ - topMargin s x) / (2 * Kd)) :
    abstainClassifier s τ y = none := by
  apply abstain_classifier_none_of_topMargin_ball;
  exact hLip;
  exact le_of_lt hKd;
  exacts [ hmargin, hradius.trans_le ( by rw [ div_le_div_iff₀ ] <;> nlinarith ) ]

end

import Mathlib

/-!
# Fixed points of selected elementary cellular automata on cyclic binary arrays

We study elementary cellular automata (ECA) acting on cyclic binary configurations
`s : Fin n → ZMod 2`.  Indices are taken cyclically using the `AddCommGroup`
structure on `Fin n` (available for `n ≠ 0`), so that `i - 1` and `i + 1` denote the
left/right neighbours of cell `i` modulo `n`.

The global update map of a local rule `g : ZMod 2 → ZMod 2 → ZMod 2 → ZMod 2` is

  `(step g s) i = g (s (i-1)) (s i) (s (i+1))`,

and a configuration `s` is a *fixed point* when `step g s = s` (`isFixed g s`).

We treat exactly four rules and give a complete classification **and exact count** of
their fixed points (throughout we assume `n ≠ 0`; the degenerate `n = 0` case is
discussed below):

* **Rule 204** (`g204 a b c = b`, the identity rule): every configuration is fixed,
  hence there are `2 ^ n` fixed points.
* **Rule 0** (`g0 a b c = 0`): the only fixed point is the zero configuration, so there
  is exactly `1` fixed point.
* **Rule 51** (`g51 a b c = 1 + b`, the global "not" rule): for `n ≠ 0` there are **no**
  fixed points.  (For `n = 0` the unique empty configuration is vacuously fixed; this is
  why we keep the `NeZero n` hypothesis rather than stating a false universal theorem.)
* **Rule 90** (`g90 a b c = a + c`): a configuration is fixed iff it satisfies the linear
  recurrence `s i = s (i-1) + s (i+1)`.  Over `ZMod 2` this forces `s (i+3) = s i`, i.e.
  every fixed point is `3`-periodic and determined by its first two cells.  The exact
  number of fixed points is

      `4`  if  `3 ∣ n`,    and    `1`  otherwise.

  Concretely: when `3 ∣ n` the four `3`-periodic patterns determined by `(s 0, s 1)`
  are all consistent with the cyclic boundary, whereas when `3 ∤ n` only the zero
  configuration closes up cyclically.
-/

namespace ECA

open scoped Fin.NatCast

variable {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]

/-- Global update map of a local ECA rule on the cyclic configuration space. -/
def step (g : ZMod 2 → ZMod 2 → ZMod 2 → ZMod 2) (s : Fin n → ZMod 2) : Fin n → ZMod 2 :=
  fun i => g (s (i - 1)) (s i) (s (i + 1))

/-- A configuration `s` is fixed by rule `g` when applying the rule leaves it unchanged. -/
def isFixed (g : ZMod 2 → ZMod 2 → ZMod 2 → ZMod 2) (s : Fin n → ZMod 2) : Prop :=
  step g s = s

/-- Rule 204: the identity rule `g204 a b c = b`. -/
def g204 (_a b _c : ZMod 2) : ZMod 2 := b

/-- Rule 0: the constant zero rule `g0 a b c = 0`. -/
def g0 (_a _b _c : ZMod 2) : ZMod 2 := 0

/-- Rule 51: the global negation rule `g51 a b c = 1 + b`. -/
def g51 (_a b _c : ZMod 2) : ZMod 2 := 1 + b

/-- Rule 90: the linear rule `g90 a b c = a + c`. -/
def g90 (a _b c : ZMod 2) : ZMod 2 := a + c

@[simp] lemma step_g204 (s : Fin n → ZMod 2) (i : Fin n) : step g204 s i = s i := rfl
@[simp] lemma step_g0 (s : Fin n → ZMod 2) (i : Fin n) : step g0 s i = 0 := rfl
@[simp] lemma step_g51 (s : Fin n → ZMod 2) (i : Fin n) : step g51 s i = 1 + s i := rfl
@[simp] lemma step_g90 (s : Fin n → ZMod 2) (i : Fin n) :
    step g90 s i = s (i - 1) + s (i + 1) := rfl

/-! ### Rule 204 -/

/-- Rule 204 acts as the identity on every configuration. -/
theorem g204_step_eq (s : Fin n → ZMod 2) : step g204 s = s := by
  funext i; simp

/-- Every configuration is a fixed point of rule 204. -/
theorem g204_isFixed (s : Fin n → ZMod 2) : isFixed g204 s := g204_step_eq s

instance : DecidablePred (isFixed g204 (n := n)) :=
  fun s => decidable_of_iff (step g204 s = s) Iff.rfl
instance : DecidablePred (isFixed g0 (n := n)) :=
  fun s => decidable_of_iff (step g0 s = s) Iff.rfl
instance : DecidablePred (isFixed g51 (n := n)) :=
  fun s => decidable_of_iff (step g51 s = s) Iff.rfl
instance : DecidablePred (isFixed g90 (n := n)) :=
  fun s => decidable_of_iff (step g90 s = s) Iff.rfl

/-- Rule 204 has exactly `2 ^ n` fixed points (all configurations). -/
theorem g204_card : Fintype.card {s : Fin n → ZMod 2 // isFixed g204 s} = 2 ^ n := by
  rw [Fintype.card_congr (Equiv.subtypeUnivEquiv g204_isFixed)]
  rw [Fintype.card_fun]
  simp

/-! ### Rule 0 -/

/-- A configuration is fixed by rule 0 iff it is the zero configuration. -/
theorem g0_isFixed_iff (s : Fin n → ZMod 2) : isFixed g0 s ↔ s = 0 := by
  unfold isFixed
  constructor
  · intro h; rw [← h]; funext i; simp
  · intro h; subst h; funext i; simp

/-- Rule 0 has exactly one fixed point. -/
theorem g0_card : Fintype.card {s : Fin n → ZMod 2 // isFixed g0 s} = 1 := by
  rw [Fintype.card_congr (Equiv.subtypeEquivRight g0_isFixed_iff)]
  exact Fintype.card_subtype_eq 0

/-! ### Rule 51 -/

/-- For `n ≠ 0`, rule 51 has no fixed points (negation cannot fix any cell). -/
theorem g51_not_isFixed (s : Fin n → ZMod 2) : ¬ isFixed g51 s := by
  intro h
  have h0 := congrFun h 0
  simp only [step_g51] at h0
  -- `1 + s 0 = s 0` is impossible in `ZMod 2`
  have hcontra : (1 : ZMod 2) = 0 := by linear_combination h0
  exact one_ne_zero hcontra

/-- Rule 51 has no fixed points: the fixed-point subtype is empty (`card = 0`). -/
theorem g51_card : Fintype.card {s : Fin n → ZMod 2 // isFixed g51 s} = 0 := by
  rw [Fintype.card_eq_zero_iff]
  exact ⟨fun p => g51_not_isFixed p.1 p.2⟩

/-! ### Rule 90

The heart of the development.  We first record the recurrence characterisation, then the
`3`-periodicity, then build the `3`-periodic patterns and count fixed points. -/

/-- A configuration is fixed by rule 90 iff it satisfies the neighbour recurrence. -/
theorem g90_isFixed_iff (s : Fin n → ZMod 2) :
    isFixed g90 s ↔ ∀ i, s i = s (i - 1) + s (i + 1) := by
  unfold isFixed
  rw [funext_iff]
  apply forall_congr'
  intro i
  rw [step_g90]
  exact eq_comm

/-- Forward form of the rule-90 recurrence: `s (i+1) = s i + s (i-1)`. -/
theorem g90_rec {s : Fin n → ZMod 2} (h : isFixed g90 s) (i : Fin n) :
    s (i + 1) = s i + s (i - 1) := by
  have hi := (g90_isFixed_iff s).1 h i
  -- `s i = s (i-1) + s (i+1)` over `ZMod 2` rearranges to the claim
  have key : ∀ x y z : ZMod 2, x = y + z → z = x + y := by decide
  exact key (s i) (s (i - 1)) (s (i + 1)) hi

/-- Over `ZMod 2` a rule-90 fixed point is `3`-periodic. -/
theorem g90_period3 {s : Fin n → ZMod 2} (h : isFixed g90 s) (i : Fin n) :
    s (i + 3) = s i := by
  have e2 := g90_rec h (i + 1)
  have e1 := g90_rec h (i + 1 + 1)
  rw [add_sub_cancel_right] at e2
  rw [add_sub_cancel_right] at e1
  have h3 : i + 3 = i + 1 + 1 + 1 := by
    have h3' : (3 : Fin n) = 1 + 1 + 1 := by norm_num
    rw [h3']; abel
  rw [h3, e1, e2]
  generalize s (i + 1) = x
  generalize s i = y
  revert x y
  decide

/-! #### The `3`-periodic pattern -/

/-- The `3`-periodic pattern with first two values `a, b` (and third value `a + b`),
indexed by a natural number via its residue modulo `3`. -/
def patt (a b : ZMod 2) (k : ℕ) : ZMod 2 :=
  if k % 3 = 0 then a else if k % 3 = 1 then b else a + b

@[simp] lemma patt_zero (a b : ZMod 2) : patt a b 0 = a := rfl
@[simp] lemma patt_one (a b : ZMod 2) : patt a b 1 = b := rfl
lemma patt_two (a b : ZMod 2) : patt a b 2 = a + b := rfl

/-- `patt` depends only on the residue modulo `3`. -/
lemma patt_mod (a b : ZMod 2) (k : ℕ) : patt a b k = patt a b (k % 3) := by
  unfold patt; rw [Nat.mod_mod_of_dvd k (dvd_refl 3)]

/-- The Fibonacci-type recurrence satisfied by `patt` over `ZMod 2`. -/
lemma patt_fib (a b : ZMod 2) (k : ℕ) :
    patt a b (k + 2) = patt a b (k + 1) + patt a b k := by
  unfold patt
  rcases (by omega : k % 3 = 0 ∨ k % 3 = 1 ∨ k % 3 = 2) with h | h | h
  · rw [show (k + 2) % 3 = 2 by omega, show (k + 1) % 3 = 1 by omega, h]; revert a b; decide
  · rw [show (k + 2) % 3 = 0 by omega, show (k + 1) % 3 = 2 by omega, h]; revert a b; decide
  · rw [show (k + 2) % 3 = 1 by omega, show (k + 1) % 3 = 0 by omega, h]; revert a b; decide

/-- The cyclic configuration of length `n` given by the `3`-periodic pattern `patt a b`. -/
def g90sol (a b : ZMod 2) : Fin n → ZMod 2 := fun i => patt a b i.val

omit [NeZero n] in
@[simp] lemma g90sol_apply (a b : ZMod 2) (i : Fin n) : g90sol a b i = patt a b i.val := rfl

lemma g90sol_zero (a b : ZMod 2) : g90sol a b (0 : Fin n) = a := by
  simp [g90sol]

lemma g90sol_one (a b : ZMod 2) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : g90sol a b (1 : Fin n) = b := by
  have h1 : (1 : Fin n).val = 1 := by
    rw [Fin.val_one']; exact Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (by omega)
  rw [g90sol_apply, h1, patt_one]

/-- Useful index lemma: `(↑k : Fin n) + 1 = ↑(k+1)`. -/
lemma fin_succ_cast (k : ℕ) : (k : Fin n) + 1 = ((k + 1 : ℕ) : Fin n) := by
  rw [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one]

/-- Useful index lemma: `(↑(k+1) : Fin n) - 1 = ↑k`. -/
lemma fin_pred_cast (k : ℕ) : ((k + 1 : ℕ) : Fin n) - 1 = (k : Fin n) := by
  rw [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one, add_sub_cancel_right]

/-- **Determination.** Every rule-90 fixed point is completely determined by its first
two cells, namely it equals the `3`-periodic pattern they generate. -/
theorem g90_determination {s : Fin n → ZMod 2} (h : isFixed g90 s) :
    s = g90sol (s 0) (s 1) := by
  have key : ∀ k : ℕ, k < n → s ((k : Fin n)) = patt (s 0) (s 1) k := by
    intro k
    induction k using Nat.strong_induction_on with
    | _ k ih =>
      rcases k with _ | _ | k
      · intro _; simp
      · intro _; simp
      · intro hk
        have hk1 : k + 1 < n := by omega
        have hk0 : k < n := by omega
        have er := g90_rec h ((k + 1 : ℕ) : Fin n)
        rw [fin_succ_cast, fin_pred_cast] at er
        rw [er, ih (k + 1) (by omega) hk1, ih k (by omega) hk0, ← patt_fib]
  funext i
  conv_lhs => rw [← Fin.cast_val_eq_self i]
  rw [key i.val i.isLt]
  rfl

/-- The cyclic index `-1` has value `n - 1`. -/
lemma neg_one_val : ((-1 : Fin n)).val = n - 1 := by
  have h0 : n ≠ 0 := NeZero.ne n
  have e : ((n - 1 : ℕ) : Fin n) + 1 = 0 := by
    rw [show ((n - 1 : ℕ) : Fin n) + 1 = ((n - 1 + 1 : ℕ) : Fin n) from by
          rw [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one], Nat.sub_add_cancel (by omega), Fin.natCast_self]
  have he : ((n - 1 : ℕ) : Fin n) = -1 := by rw [eq_neg_iff_add_eq_zero]; exact e
  rw [← he, Fin.val_natCast, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (by omega)]

/-- The cyclic index `-2` has value `n - 2` (for `n ≥ 2`). -/
lemma neg_two_val (hn2 : 2 ≤ n) : ((-2 : Fin n)).val = n - 2 := by
  have e : ((n - 2 : ℕ) : Fin n) + 2 = 0 := by
    rw [show ((n - 2 : ℕ) : Fin n) + 2 = ((n - 2 + 2 : ℕ) : Fin n) from by
          rw [Nat.cast_add]; norm_num, Nat.sub_add_cancel hn2, Fin.natCast_self]
  have he : ((n - 2 : ℕ) : Fin n) = -2 := by rw [eq_neg_iff_add_eq_zero]; exact e

/-- With `3 ∣ n`, the right neighbour shifts the residue by `+1`. -/
lemma val_succ_mod3 (hd : 3 ∣ n) (i : Fin n) : (i + 1).val % 3 = (i.val + 1) % 3 := by
  have h0 : n ≠ 0 := NeZero.ne n
  have hn : 2 ≤ n := by rcases hd with ⟨k, rfl⟩; omega
  rw [Fin.val_add, Fin.val_one', Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (show (1 : ℕ) < n by omega),
      Nat.mod_mod_of_dvd _ hd]

/-- With `3 ∣ n`, the left neighbour shifts the residue by `+2`. -/
lemma val_pred_mod3 (hd : 3 ∣ n) (i : Fin n) : (i - 1).val % 3 = (i.val + 2) % 3 := by
  have h0 : n ≠ 0 := NeZero.ne n
  rw [sub_eq_add_neg, Fin.val_add, neg_one_val, Nat.mod_mod_of_dvd _ hd]
  rcases hd with ⟨k, rfl⟩

These conjectures are distilled from the v16a research cycle in
`Computation/ECAFixedVariety.lean` and `Computation/ECALinearSubspace.lean`.

The cycle established two anchor facts:

* **Refutation.** The Turing-complete Wolfram Rule 110 has a *single* fixed point
  (the all-zero configuration) for every length `n ≥ 1`, hence fixed-point-variety
  dimension `0` — the *minimum* among nonempty varieties — directly falsifying the
  conjecture "Turing-complete ⇒ maximal fixed-point dimension"
  (`complexity_dimension_conjecture_false`).
* **Structure.** For *linear* (additive) rules the fixed-point set is literally the
  kernel of `step − id`, a `GF(2)`-subspace, so it always has `2^k` points
  (`linearFixed_card_pow_two`); Rule 110 is provably nonlinear (`g110_not_linear`).

The fixed-point variety is therefore a real GF(2) scheme, but its dimension is the
*wrong* complexity invariant. The directions below propose the right one.

---

## Direction 1 — Spacetime entropy, not fixed-point dimension, tracks complexity.

**Conjecture.** Define the *spacetime subshift* `Σ_r` of rule `r` as the set of valid
bi-infinite orbit diagrams, an SFT over the de Bruijn graph. Its topological entropy
`h(Σ_r) = lim (1/n) log #(period-n columns)` separates Wolfram's classes:
`h = 0` for Class 1/2, `h > 0` for Class 3, and Class 4 (e.g. Rule 110) sits exactly
at the `h = 0` boundary while supporting unbounded transients.

**The key insight is** that Turing-completeness lives in the *transient orbit
structure* (gliders, collisions), which the static fixed-point variety throws away;
the spacetime SFT retains it and its entropy is the genuine invariant.

**Why now?** This cycle proved the fixed-point count of Rule 110 is constantly `1`,
so any complexity invariant *must* be orbit-based, not equilibrium-based. The
transfer-matrix machinery for counting period-`n` configurations (`tr(T^n)`) is
already formalizable in Mathlib (`Matrix.trace`, `Matrix.pow`), giving an immediate
attack route.

**Conjecture.** For every rule `r` there is an explicit `0/1` matrix `T_r` indexed by
2-cell windows such that `Nat.card {s : Config n // isFixed (g r) s} = trace (T_rⁿ)`,
and the asymptotic growth rate equals the Perron eigenvalue `ρ(T_r)`; the variety
"dimension" is `log₂ ρ(T_r)`, a rule-intrinsic real number.

**The key insight is** that the fixed-point set is a *subshift of finite type*, so its
cardinality is governed by a transfer matrix exactly as in statistical mechanics —
turning a combinatorial count into linear algebra.

**Why now?** We verified the pattern computationally (Rule 90: `1,1,4,1,1,4,…`,
period-3 because `ρ` has a cube-root-of-unity spectrum; Rule 204: `2^n` because
`ρ = 2`). Proving `#fix = tr(Tⁿ)` for the five formalized rules is a finite, bounded
target that would convert every numeric observation in the Lab Notes into a theorem.

**Conjecture.** The Rule 90 fixed-point subspace `linearFixed 1 0 1` over `Config n`
has dimension `> 0` if and only if `3 ∣ n`; equivalently the circulant operator
`x ↦ x_{i-1} + x_{i+1} − x_i` is singular over `GF(2)` exactly when `3 ∣ n`. More
generally the dimension equals `deg gcd(t² + t + 1, tⁿ − 1)` in `GF(2)[t]`.

**The key insight is** that a linear ECA's fixed-point dimension is a *cyclotomic*
quantity: it counts roots of the rule's characteristic polynomial among the `n`-th
roots of unity, so number theory (orders mod small primes) governs the geometry.

**Why now?** We proved a nonzero fixed point exists at `n = 3`
(`rule90_nontrivial_fixed_three`) and `linearFixed_card_pow_two` already exposes the
dimension as `finrank`. Mathlib's `Polynomial.cyclotomic` and circulant-matrix
support make the gcd characterization directly reachable.

**Conjecture.** A rule `r` is GF(2)-linear iff its fixed-point variety is closed under
addition for *all* lengths `n` simultaneously; a single length can fail (the converse
gap noted by the Critic: Rule 0 and Rule 110 both give count `1 = 2⁰` yet only Rule 0
is linear). Precisely: `(∀ n, IsSubmodule (fixed r n)) ↔ r ∈ {0,60,90,102,150,170,204,240,…}`
(the 8 additive rules and their reflections).

**The key insight is** that linearity is a *global* property of the whole tower of
varieties `{V_n}`, not of any single `V_n` — closure-at-one-`n` is necessary but not
sufficient, which is why our safe-direction lemma (`g110_not_linear`) certifies
nonlinearity pointwise rather than from a single count.

**Why now?** This cycle isolated the exact converse counterexample (count `1` is
realized by both a linear and a nonlinear rule), so the precise boundary is known and
ready to be formalized as an `Iff` over the finite catalogue of additive rules.

**Conjecture.** A rule with affine ANF `f = ℓ(a,b,c) + 1` (a linear part plus the
constant `1`, e.g. Rule 51 `= b + 1`) has fixed-point variety either empty or a
*coset* of `linearFixed ℓ`; it is empty exactly when `1 ∉ image(ℓ − id)`. Thus the
empty variety (`rule51_not_isFixed`) is the GF(2) shadow of an unsolvable affine
system, and `#fix ∈ {0} ∪ {2^k}`.

into an *affine* solution set, so the dichotomy "empty vs. power-of-two coset" is the
Rouché–Capelli theorem over `GF(2)` applied to cellular automata.

as the inconsistency of an affine GF(2) system, via Mathlib's `LinearMap.range` and
coset API, would unify the linear (Direction 1–3) and degenerate cases under one
solvability criterion.

# Torsor of Isomorphisms: The Ambiguity of Structural Translation

## Research Objective

Formalize and prove that the collection of isomorphisms between two isomorphic objects forms a torsor for the automorphism group. This makes precise the 'isomorphism of isomorphisms' concept: different isomorphisms between the same structures are different translation dictionaries, and the automorphism group quantifies the semantic ambiguity.

## Key Definitions

1. **isoTorsor**: Given a category C and objects X Y : C with an isomorphism between them, define the action of Aut X on Iso X Y by post-composition, and prove it forms a MulActionTorsor (i.e., the action is free and transitive).

2. **isoCardinality**: Prove that for isomorphic objects X ≅ Y, the cardinality of Iso X Y equals the cardinality of Aut X (and of Aut Y), establishing that automorphisms measure the number of distinct 'translations.'

## Main Theorems

1. **iso_torsor_aut**: For any two isomorphic objects X, Y in a category C, the type Iso X Y forms a torsor for the group Aut X under the action (σ : Aut X) • (f : Iso X Y) = σ.hom ≫ f.

2. **iso_torsor_aut'**: Dually, Iso X Y forms a torsor for Aut Y under pre-composition: (τ : Aut Y) • (f : Iso X Y) = f ≫ τ.hom.

3. **zmod2_ring_aut_trivial**: The automorphism group of ZMod 2 as a commutative ring is trivial (the only ring automorphism is identity). Consequence: there is exactly one ring isomorphism between ZMod 2 and ZMod 2.

4. **fin2_type_aut_swap**: The automorphism group of Fin 2 as a type (i.e., Equiv.Perm (Fin 2)) has exactly 2 elements: identity and the swap. Consequence: there are exactly 2 type isomorphisms between Fin 2 and Fin 2.

5. **add_group_int_aut_negation**: The automorphism group of (ℤ, +) as an additive group has exactly 2 elements: identity and negation. These preserve all first-order group properties but represent different 'translations' — negation maps positive elements to negative ones, a distinction invisible to the group theory.

## Proof Strategy

- For the general theorem: Use CategoryTheory.Iso and CategoryTheory.Aut from Mathlib. The key lemma is that for any two isomorphisms f g : Iso X Y, there exists a unique σ : Aut X such that g = σ.hom ≫ f. Prove existence (σ = f.inv ≫ g) and uniqueness (by cancellation).
- For concrete examples: Use `decide` and `fin_cases` for finite structures. For ZMod 2, case-split on the two elements and use ring axioms. For Fin 2, enumerate permutations. For ℤ, use the fact that additive group endomorphisms of ℤ are determined by the image of 1.
- For the 'meaning vs truth' interpretation: Show that the negation automorphism of (ℤ, +) preserves all group-theoretic properties but does not preserve the order relation (n > 0), demonstrating a property that is invariant under isomorphism in the category of ordered groups but not in the category of groups.

This formalizes the philosophical observation that isomorphic structures can carry different 'meanings' in a mathematically precise way: the torsor Iso X Y has multiple elements precisely when Aut X is nontrivial, and each element represents a different way to 'translate' X into Y. The automorphism group measures how many such translations exist.

/-!
# Boolean Logic *is* the Field 𝔽₂: a Ring Isomorphism

Research theme: *Isomorphisms of Meaning — When Structures Collide.*

Companion to `Bridges.StructuralCollisions`. There we saw that a single algebraic axiom
(`x*x = x`) forces a *new* (order/lattice) structure to appear. Here we exhibit the
sharpest possible "collision of meaning": two structures that were defined for completely
different purposes — *propositional logic* (`Bool` with `xor`/`and`) and *finite field
arithmetic* (`ZMod 2`) — are literally the **same** object, witnessed by an explicit ring
isomorphism `Bool ≃+* ZMod 2`.

Mathlib already equips `Bool` with a `CommRing` structure (through `BooleanRing.toCommRing`)
in which `+ = xor` and `* = and`. We:

* construct `BooleanLogicField.boolRingEquiv : Bool ≃+* ZMod 2`;
* record the dictionary `xor ↔ (+)` and `and ↔ (*)` it induces
  (`boolRingEquiv_xor`, `boolRingEquiv_and`);
* prove the field-defining fact that every nonzero `Bool` is a unit
  (`bool_nonzero_isUnit`), exhibiting `Bool` as a (two-element) field — the same field
  `ZMod 2` is, transported across the isomorphism.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
-- Hypothesis H3: the `CommRing Bool` instance Mathlib derives from the Boolean-algebra
--   structure is *the field 𝔽₂*, i.e. there is a ring isomorphism `Bool ≃+* ZMod 2`.
-- Experiment: define the obvious bijection `false ↦ 0`, `true ↦ 1` and check the ring-hom
--   laws. Because both carriers are finite with `DecidableEq`, *all four* `RingEquiv`
--   obligations (`left_inv`, `right_inv`, `map_mul'`, `map_add'`) discharge by `decide`.
--   Confirmed H3 with a fully `decide`-checked isomorphism (axioms: propext/choice/Quot).
-- Insight: under this single map, the truth-table of `xor` *is* the addition table of
--   𝔽₂ and the truth-table of `and` *is* its multiplication table. "Exclusive-or = plus"
--   and "and = times" are not analogies; they are one equality read in two languages —
--   the cleanest possible "isomorphism of meaning".
-- Cross-link: `and` is idempotent, so `Bool` is a Boolean ring; the abstract results of
--   `Bridges.StructuralCollisions` (forced commutativity, characteristic two, product =
--   meet) therefore specialise to `Bool`, and the meet `a ⊓ b` of the induced order is
--   exactly `a && b`.
-- Failure analysis: stating the dictionary lemmas with `xor a b` on the left first looked
--   like it needed a rewrite, but `a + b = xor a b` holds by `rfl`, so `map_add` applies
--   directly; the apparent mismatch was purely notational.
-/

namespace BooleanLogicField

/-- The canonical ring isomorphism between propositional logic (`Bool` with `xor`/`and`)
and the finite field `ZMod 2`. It sends `false ↦ 0` and `true ↦ 1`; every ring-equivalence
obligation is decided by finite case analysis. -/
def boolRingEquiv : Bool ≃+* ZMod 2 where
  toFun b := if b then 1 else 0
  invFun z := if z = 1 then true else false
  left_inv := by decide
  right_inv := by decide
  map_mul' := by decide
  map_add' := by decide

@[simp] theorem boolRingEquiv_true : boolRingEquiv true = 1 := by decide

@[simp] theorem boolRingEquiv_false : boolRingEquiv false = 0 := by decide

/-- **`xor` is addition.** The image of an exclusive-or under the isomorphism is the sum
of the images in `ZMod 2`. -/
theorem boolRingEquiv_xor (a b : Bool) :
    boolRingEquiv (xor a b) = boolRingEquiv a + boolRingEquiv b :=
  boolRingEquiv.map_add a b

/-- **`and` is multiplication.** The image of a conjunction under the isomorphism is the
product of the images in `ZMod 2`. -/
theorem boolRingEquiv_and (a b : Bool) :
    boolRingEquiv (a && b) = boolRingEquiv a * boolRingEquiv b :=
  boolRingEquiv.map_mul a b

/-- On `Bool`, ring addition is exactly exclusive-or. -/
theorem bool_add_eq_xor (a b : Bool) : a + b = xor a b := rfl

/-- On `Bool`, ring multiplication is exactly conjunction. -/
theorem bool_mul_eq_and (a b : Bool) : a * b = (a && b) := rfl

/-- **`Bool` is a field.** Every nonzero element is a unit: the only nonzero element is
`true`, and `true * true = true = 1`. This is the field property of `ZMod 2` transported
across `boolRingEquiv`. -/
theorem bool_nonzero_isUnit : ∀ a : Bool, a ≠ 0 → ∃ b : Bool, a * b = 1 := by decide

/-- The isomorphism is, in particular, a bijection: `Bool` and `ZMod 2` have the same two
elements, identified canonically. -/
theorem boolRingEquiv_bijective : Function.Bijective boolRingEquiv :=
  boolRingEquiv.bijective

/-- `&&` is idempotent, so `Bool` is a Boolean ring in the sense of
`Bridges.StructuralCollisions`. -/
theorem bool_idem (x : Bool) : x * x = x := by cases x <;> decide

/-- **Cross-link to `StructuralCollisions`.** Specialising the abstract "product = meet"
result `StructuralCollisions.mul_isGLB` to `Bool`, conjunction `a && b` is exactly the
greatest lower bound of `{a, b}` in the product-induced order. Thus the order-theoretic
meet, the ring product, and logical `and` all coincide on `Bool`. -/

    StructuralCollisions.le (a && b) a ∧ StructuralCollisions.le (a && b) b ∧
      ∀ c, StructuralCollisions.le c a → StructuralCollisions.le c b →
        StructuralCollisions.le c (a && b) := by
  have h := StructuralCollisions.mul_isGLB bool_idem a b
  simpa [bool_mul_eq_and] using h

end BooleanLogicField

import Mathlib

/-!
# Structural Collisions: Isomorphisms of Meaning

Research theme: *Isomorphisms of Meaning — When Structures Collide.*

This file studies a recurring phenomenon: imposing a single, innocent-looking axiom on
one structure forces a *second*, a priori unrelated structure to appear — and the two
structures turn out to encode the *same* information. The product in a Boolean ring
*is* the meet of an order; characteristic two appears for free; and an idempotent
ring's multiplication *is* a meet-semilattice operation. These are "isomorphisms of
meaning": one syntactic operation acquiring two semantic readings.

We work axiomatically over an arbitrary (not-assumed-commutative) ring `R` satisfying the
single idempotence law `∀ x, x * x = x` (a *Boolean ring*), and show:

* `StructuralCollisions.add_self` : characteristic two emerges, `a + a = 0`.
* `StructuralCollisions.mul_comm'` : commutativity is *forced* (Boolean rings are
  commutative).
* the induced relation `a ≤ b ↔ a * b = a` is a partial order (`refl/antisymm/trans`);
* `StructuralCollisions.mul_isGLB` : the ring product `a * b` **is** the greatest lower
  bound of `{a, b}` in that order — the algebraic and order-theoretic meanings coincide.

We then specialise everything to `ZMod 2` as a concrete collision witness.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
-- Hypothesis H1: a single idempotence axiom `x*x = x` collapses a ring's degrees of
--   freedom enough to *force* both characteristic two and commutativity.
-- Experiment: the classic two-line arguments
--     a+a = (a+a)^2 = 4a  ⟹  2a = 0;
--     a+b = (a+b)^2 = a + ab + ba + b  ⟹  ab + ba = 0  ⟹  (char 2) ab = ba.
--   Both went through. Confirmed H1.
-- Hypothesis H2 ("collision of meaning"): the *product* and the order-theoretic *meet*
--   of the induced order are literally the same function. Verified via the explicit
--   GLB characterisation `mul_isGLB`.
-- Insight: the order `a ≤ b ↔ a*b = a` only becomes antisymmetric *after* commutativity
--   is available; so H2 genuinely depends on H1. The structures do not merely coexist —
--   the richer (order/lattice) structure is *derived from*, and pinned down by, the
--   algebraic axiom. That derivation is the "isomorphism of meaning".
-- Failure analysis 1: an early skeleton made `idem` a parameter of the `def le`, which
--   it does not use; Lean then mis-parsed `le idem a b`. Fix: `le` depends only on `a b`;
--   the `idem` hypothesis is threaded only through the theorems that need it.
-- Failure analysis 2: defining `≤` as the dual `a*b = b` makes `*` the *join* instead,
--   and the GLB statement fails. Orientation matters; convention fixed to `a*b = a`.
-/

namespace StructuralCollisions

/- A `Boolean ring`-style hypothesis bundle: a ring whose every element is idempotent
under multiplication. We keep it as a plain hypothesis on a generic ring so the results
are self-contained and do not depend on Mathlib's `BooleanRing` typeclass. -/
variable {R : Type*} [Ring R] (idem : ∀ x : R, x * x = x)

/-- The order induced by the product: `a ≤ b` means `a` is "below" `b`, i.e. `a * b = a`.
This definition does not need the idempotence hypothesis; that hypothesis enters only when
proving the order axioms. -/
def le (a b : R) : Prop := a * b = a

include idem

/-
**Characteristic two emerges.** In a Boolean ring every element is its own additive
inverse, i.e. `a + a = 0`.
-/
theorem add_self (a : R) : a + a = 0 := by
  -- By the distributive property, we have $(a + a) * (a + a) = a * (a + a) + a * (a + a)$.
  have h_dist : (a + a) * (a + a) = a * (a + a) + a * (a + a) := by
    rw [ add_mul ];
  simp_all +decide [ mul_add ]

/-
**Commutativity is forced.** Every Boolean ring is commutative.
-/
theorem mul_comm' (a b : R) : a * b = b * a := by
  -- Expand `idem (a+b)` to `a + a*b + (b*a + b) = a + b`, giving `a*b + b*a = 0`.
  have h := idem (a + b)
  have hx : (a + b) * (a + b) = a + a * b + (b * a + b) := by
    rw [mul_add, add_mul, add_mul, idem a, idem b]; abel
  rw [hx] at h
  have key : a * b + b * a = 0 := by
    have t : a * b + b * a = (a + a * b + (b * a + b)) - (a + b) := by abel
    rw [t, h, sub_self]
  -- Characteristic two (`add_self`) turns `a*b + b*a = 0` into `a*b = b*a`.
  have hbb := add_self idem (b * a)
  have e : a * b + b * a = b * a + b * a := by rw [key, hbb]
  exact add_right_cancel e

theorem le_refl' (a : R) : le a a := by
  exact idem a

theorem le_antisymm' {a b : R} (hab : le a b) (hba : le b a) : a = b := by
  convert hab.symm using 1;
  convert hba.symm using 1;
  convert mul_comm' idem a b using 1

/- Transitivity needs only associativity, *not* idempotence, so we `omit idem`: the order
axiom here is inherited from the bare ring structure. -/
omit idem in
theorem le_trans' {a b c : R} (hab : le a b) (hbc : le b c) : le a c := by
  grind +locals

/-
`a * b ≤ a` in the induced order.
-/
theorem mul_le_left (a b : R) : le (a * b) a := by
  have h_comm : (a * b) * a = a * (b * a) := by
    rw [ mul_assoc ];
  have h_comm : (a * b) * a = a * (a * b) := by
    convert h_comm using 1;
    exact congr_arg _ ( mul_comm' idem a b );
  simp_all +decide [ ← mul_assoc ];
  exact h_comm

/-
`a * b ≤ b` in the induced order.
-/
theorem mul_le_right (a b : R) : le (a * b) b := by
  unfold le;
  rw [ mul_assoc, idem ]

/-
Any common lower bound of `a` and `b` is below `a * b`.
-/
/- Like transitivity, the "dominates every common lower bound" half of the GLB property
needs only associativity, not idempotence. -/
omit idem in
theorem le_mul_of_le_of_le {a b c : R} (hca : le c a) (hcb : le c b) :
    le c (a * b) := by
      unfold le at *;
      grind

/-- **The collision of meaning.** The ring product `a * b` is exactly the greatest lower
bound of `{a, b}` in the induced order: it is a lower bound of both `a` and `b`, and it
dominates every common lower bound. The algebraic operation and the order-theoretic meet
are the *same* function. -/
theorem mul_isGLB (a b : R) :
    le (a * b) a ∧ le (a * b) b ∧ ∀ c, le c a → le c b → le c (a * b) :=
  ⟨mul_le_left idem a b, mul_le_right idem a b,
    fun _ hca hcb => le_mul_of_le_of_le hca hcb⟩

end StructuralCollisions

namespace StructuralCollisions

/-! ## Concrete collision witness: `ZMod 2`

`ZMod 2` satisfies the idempotence law, so all of the above applies. We record the
witness explicitly. -/

theorem zmod2_idem : ∀ x : ZMod 2, x * x = x := by
  decide

/-- The forced commutativity, instantiated at `ZMod 2`. -/
theorem zmod2_mul_comm (a b : ZMod 2) : a * b = b * a := mul_comm' zmod2_idem a b

/-- Characteristic two, instantiated at `ZMod 2`. -/
theorem zmod2_add_self (a : ZMod 2) : a + a = 0 := add_self zmod2_idem a

end StructuralCollisions

/-!
# Conditionally negative semidefinite kernels, separation kernels, and ultrametrics

This file develops, in a fully finite and self-contained way, the notion of a
**conditionally negative semidefinite** (CNSD) kernel `K : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ`,
proves the basic closure properties (addition, nonnegative scaling, nonnegative
finite combinations), proves the **separation/partition kernel** lemma, and uses
it to show that every finite **ultrametric** taking values in `{0, 1, …, m}` is
CNSD.

The main results are:

* `CNSD_separation` : for any coloring `f : Fin n → β`, the kernel
  `K_f i j = if f i = f j then 0 else 1` is CNSD.  The proof uses the exact
  quadratic identity packaged in `block_sum_sq`.
* `CNSD_cut` : for an ultrametric `d` and threshold `t > 0`, the cut kernel
  `if d i j < t then 0 else 1` is CNSD (it is a separation kernel for the
  threshold partition `i ~ j ↔ d i j < t`).
* `CNSD_ultrametric_int` : every finite ultrametric whose values lie in
  `{0, 1, …, m}` is CNSD, via the telescoping layer-cake decomposition into cut
  kernels.
-/

open Finset BigOperators

namespace UltrametricCNSD

/-- A finite kernel `K : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ` is **conditionally negative
semidefinite** if every zero-sum vector `x` makes the quadratic form
`∑ᵢⱼ xᵢ xⱼ K i j` nonpositive. -/
def CNSD {n : ℕ} (K : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, (∑ i, x i = 0) → ∑ i, ∑ j, x i * x j * K i j ≤ 0

/-! ## Closure properties of CNSD -/

/-- The zero kernel is CNSD. -/
lemma CNSD_zero {n : ℕ} : CNSD (fun _ _ : Fin n => (0 : ℝ)) := by
  exact fun x _ => by simp +decide ;

/-- CNSD is closed under addition of kernels. -/
lemma CNSD.add {n : ℕ} {K L : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ} (hK : CNSD K) (hL : CNSD L) :
    CNSD (fun i j => K i j + L i j) := by
      exact fun x hx => by simpa only [ mul_add, Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.mul_sum ] using add_nonpos ( hK x hx ) ( hL x hx ) ;

/-- CNSD is closed under multiplication by a nonnegative scalar. -/
lemma CNSD.smul_nonneg {n : ℕ} {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) {K : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ}
    (hK : CNSD K) : CNSD (fun i j => c * K i j) := by
      intro x hx; convert mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos hc ( hK x hx ) using 1; simp +decide [ Finset.mul_sum _ _ _, mul_assoc, mul_left_comm ]

/-- CNSD is closed under nonnegative finite combinations of kernels. -/
lemma CNSD_sum {n : ℕ} {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (c : ι → ℝ)
    (K : ι → Fin n → Fin n → ℝ) (hc : ∀ t ∈ s, 0 ≤ c t)
    (hK : ∀ t ∈ s, CNSD (K t)) :
    CNSD (fun i j => ∑ t ∈ s, c t * K t i j) := by
      intro x hx;
      -- By Fubini's theorem, we can interchange the order of summation.
      have h_fubini : ∑ i, ∑ j, x i * x j * (∑ t ∈ s, c t * K t i j) = ∑ t ∈ s, c t * (∑ i, ∑ j, x i * x j * K t i j) := by
        simp +decide only [Finset.mul_sum _ _ _, mul_left_comm];
        exact Eq.symm ( by rw [ Finset.sum_comm ] ; exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun _ _ => Finset.sum_comm );
      exact h_fubini.symm ▸ Finset.sum_nonpos fun t ht => mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos ( hc t ht ) ( hK t ht x hx )

/-! ## Separation / partition kernels -/

/-- **Block-sum identity.** The "same-fiber" indicator quadratic form is the sum
over colors of squared block sums. -/
lemma block_sum_sq {n : ℕ} {β : Type*} [DecidableEq β] (f : Fin n → β)
    (x : Fin n → ℝ) :
    (∑ i, ∑ j, x i * x j * (if f i = f j then (1 : ℝ) else 0))
      = ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.image f,
          (∑ i ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun i => f i = a), x i) ^ 2 := by
            simp +decide [ sq, Finset.sum_ite ];

theorem CNSD_separation {n : ℕ} {β : Type*} [DecidableEq β] (f : Fin n → β) :
    CNSD (fun i j => if f i = f j then (0 : ℝ) else 1) := by
      intro x hx
      have h_if : ∀ i j, (if f i = f j then 0 else 1 : ℝ) = 1 - (if f i = f j then 1 else 0) := by
        grind
      simp_all +decide;
      simp +decide only [mul_sub, mul_one, sum_sub_distrib];
      simp +decide only [← Finset.mul_sum _ _ _, hx, ← sum_mul, zero_mul, block_sum_sq];
      exact sub_nonpos_of_le ( Finset.sum_nonneg fun _ _ => sq_nonneg _ )

/-! ## Finite ultrametrics -/

/-- A finite ultrametric on `Fin n`. -/
structure IsUltrametric {n : ℕ} (d : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ) : Prop where
  refl : ∀ i, d i i = 0
  symm : ∀ i j, d i j = d j i
  nonneg : ∀ i j, 0 ≤ d i j
  ultra : ∀ i j k, d i k ≤ max (d i j) (d j k)

/-- The canonical representative of `i` at threshold `t`: the least index `j`
(in `Fin n`) with `d i j < t`.  Falls back to `i` when the set is empty (which
does not happen for `t > 0`). -/
noncomputable def reprAt {n : ℕ} (d : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ) (t : ℝ) (i : Fin n) :
    Fin n :=
  if h : (Finset.univ.filter (fun j => d i j < t)).Nonempty then
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun j => d i j < t)).min' h
  else i

/-- For an ultrametric and `t > 0`, two points get the same threshold
representative iff they are within distance `< t`. -/
lemma reprAt_eq_iff {n : ℕ} {d : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ} (hd : IsUltrametric d)
    {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) (i j : Fin n) :
    reprAt d t i = reprAt d t j ↔ d i j < t := by
      constructor;
      · intro h_eq;
        -- By definition of `reprAt`, we know that `d i (reprAt d t i) < t` and `d j (reprAt d t j) < t`.
        have h_repr_i : d i (reprAt d t i) < t := by
          unfold reprAt;
          split_ifs with h;
          · exact Finset.mem_filter.mp ( Finset.min'_mem _ h ) |>.2;
          · exact lt_of_le_of_lt ( hd.refl i ▸ le_rfl ) ht
        have h_repr_j : d j (reprAt d t j) < t := by
          unfold reprAt;
          split_ifs <;> simp_all +decide [ Finset.min' ];
          · exact Finset.mem_filter.mp ( Finset.min'_mem _ ‹_› ) |>.2;
          · linarith [ hd.refl j ];
        have := hd.ultra i ( reprAt d t i ) j; simp_all +decide [ hd.symm ] ;
        cases this <;> linarith;
      · intro hij
        have h_eq : Finset.univ.filter (fun k => d i k < t) = Finset.univ.filter (fun k => d j k < t) := by
          ext k;
          constructor <;> intro hk <;> have := hd.ultra i j k <;> have := hd.ultra j i k <;> simp_all +decide [ hd.symm ]; all_goals grind;
        have h_nonempty : (Finset.univ.filter (fun k => d i k < t)).Nonempty := by
          exact ⟨ j, by simpa using hij ⟩;
        unfold reprAt; aesop;

/-- For an ultrametric and `t > 0`, the cut kernel `if d i j < t then 0 else 1`
is CNSD: it is the separation kernel of the threshold partition. -/
lemma CNSD_cut {n : ℕ} {d : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ} (hd : IsUltrametric d) {t : ℝ}
    (ht : 0 < t) :
    CNSD (fun i j => if d i j < t then (0 : ℝ) else 1) := by
      convert CNSD_separation ( fun i => reprAt d t i ) using 1;
      ext i j; simp +decide [ reprAt_eq_iff hd ht i j ] ;

/-- **Integer layer-cake identity.** For a real value `w = k` with `k ≤ m`,
summing the cut indicators over thresholds `1, …, m` recovers `w`. -/
lemma int_layer {m : ℕ} {w : ℝ} {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ m) (hw : w = (k : ℝ)) :
    (∑ t ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m, (if w < (t : ℝ) then (0 : ℝ) else 1)) = w := by
      simp_all +decide [ Finset.sum_ite ];
      convert Nat.card_Icc 1 k using 2;
      grind

/-- **Ultrametric CNSD (integer-valued form).** Every finite ultrametric whose
values lie in `{0, 1, …, m}` is conditionally negative semidefinite. -/
theorem CNSD_ultrametric_int {n m : ℕ} {d : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ}
    (hd : IsUltrametric d) (hval : ∀ i j, ∃ k : ℕ, k ≤ m ∧ d i j = (k : ℝ)) :
    CNSD d := by
      convert CNSD_sum ( Finset.Icc 1 m ) ( fun _ => 1 ) ( fun t i j => if d i j < t then ( 0 : ℝ ) else 1 ) _ _ using 1;
      · ext i j; obtain ⟨ k, hk₁, hk₂ ⟩ := hval i j; simp +decide [ hk₂ ] ;
        erw [ Finset.sum_Ico_eq_sum_range ] ; norm_num [ Finset.sum_range_succ' ];
        rw [ ← Finset.sum_range_add_sum_Ico _ ( show k ≤ m from hk₁ ) ] ; norm_num [ add_comm, Finset.sum_Ico_eq_sum_range ];
        rw [ Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x hx => if_neg ( by linarith [ Finset.mem_range.mp hx ] ) ] ; norm_num;
      · norm_num;
      · exact fun t ht => CNSD_cut hd ( Nat.cast_pos.mpr <| Finset.mem_Icc.mp ht |>.1 )

end UltrametricCNSD

open Finset

namespace HyperRamsey

variable {n : ℕ}

subsets are mathematically relevant. -/
abbrev Coloring (n : ℕ) := Finset (Fin n) → Bool

/-- `S` is a monochromatic clique of color `b` for the `r`-uniform coloring `c`
when every `r`-element subset of `S` receives color `b`. -/
def IsMonoClique (r : ℕ) (c : Coloring n) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (b : Bool) : Prop :=
  ∀ T ∈ S.powersetCard r, c T = b

`r`-subsets of `Fin n` contains a red `k`-clique or a blue `l`-clique. -/
def HyperRamseyProp (r n k l : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ c : Coloring n,
    (∃ S : Finset (Fin n), S.card = k ∧ IsMonoClique r c S true) ∨
    (∃ S : Finset (Fin n), S.card = l ∧ IsMonoClique r c S false)

/-- Subsets of a monochromatic clique are monochromatic cliques of the same
color. -/
theorem IsMonoClique.subset {r : ℕ} {c : Coloring n} {S T : Finset (Fin n)}

    IsMonoClique r c T b := by
  intro U hU
  rw [Finset.mem_powersetCard] at hU
  exact h U (Finset.mem_powersetCard.mpr ⟨hU.1.trans hTS, hU.2⟩)

    HyperRamseyProp r n l k := by
  intro c
  rcases h (fun T => !(c T)) with ⟨S, hS, hmono⟩ | ⟨S, hS, hmono⟩
  · refine Or.inr ⟨S, hS, ?_⟩
    intro T hT
    have := hmono T hT
    simpa using this
  · refine Or.inl ⟨S, hS, ?_⟩
    intro T hT
    have := hmono T hT
    simpa using this

theorem hyperRamsey_mono_clique {r n k l : ℕ}
    (h : HyperRamseyProp r n (k + 1) (l + 1)) :
    HyperRamseyProp r n k l := by
  intro c
  rcases h c with ⟨S, hS, hmono⟩ | ⟨S, hS, hmono⟩
  · obtain ⟨T, hTS, hTcard⟩ := Finset.exists_subset_card_eq (show k ≤ S.card by omega)
    exact Or.inl ⟨T, hTcard, hmono.subset hTS⟩
  · obtain ⟨T, hTS, hTcard⟩ := Finset.exists_subset_card_eq (show l ≤ S.card by omega)
    exact Or.inr ⟨T, hTcard, hmono.subset hTS⟩

/-- **Monotonicity in the number of vertices**: more vertices can only make the
Ramsey property easier to satisfy.  A clique found in the first `n` vertices is
transported along the canonical embedding `Fin n ↪ Fin m`. -/
theorem hyperRamsey_mono_vertices {r n m k l : ℕ} (hnm : n ≤ m)
    (h : HyperRamseyProp r n k l) :
    HyperRamseyProp r m k l := by
  intro c
  set e : Fin n ↪ Fin m := (Fin.castLEEmb hnm)
  set c' : Coloring n := fun T => c (T.map e) with hc'
  have key : ∀ (S : Finset (Fin n)) (b : Bool), IsMonoClique r c' S b →
      IsMonoClique r c (S.map e) b := by
    intro S b hmono U hU
    rw [Finset.mem_powersetCard] at hU
    obtain ⟨hUsub, hUcard⟩ := hU
    obtain ⟨U', hU'sub, rfl⟩ : ∃ U' : Finset (Fin n), U' ⊆ S ∧ U'.map e = U := by
      refine ⟨S.filter (fun x => e x ∈ U), Finset.filter_subset _ _, ?_⟩
      ext y
      simp only [Finset.mem_map, Finset.mem_filter]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨a, ⟨_, ha2⟩, rfl⟩; exact ha2
      · intro hy
        obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_map.mp (hUsub hy)
        exact ⟨a, ⟨ha, by simpa using hy⟩, rfl⟩
    have : c' U' = b :=
      hmono U' (Finset.mem_powersetCard.mpr ⟨hU'sub, by simpa [Finset.card_map] using hUcard⟩)
    simpa [hc'] using this
  rcases h c' with ⟨S, hS, hmono⟩ | ⟨S, hS, hmono⟩
  · exact Or.inl ⟨S.map e, by simp [Finset.card_map, hS], key S true hmono⟩
  · exact Or.inr ⟨S.map e, by simp [Finset.card_map, hS], key S false hmono⟩

/-- **Degenerate regime**: when the requested clique size is below the
uniformity, the red clique condition is vacuous (a set of fewer than `r`
vertices spans no `r`-edge), so the Ramsey property holds as soon as there are
`k` vertices. -/
theorem hyperRamsey_lt_uniformity {r n k l : ℕ} (hkr : k < r) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
    HyperRamseyProp r n k l := by
  intro c
  obtain ⟨S, hS, hScard⟩ :=
    Finset.exists_subset_card_eq (show k ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).card by simpa using hkn)
  refine Or.inl ⟨S, hScard, ?_⟩
  intro T hT
  rw [Finset.mem_powersetCard] at hT
  have : T.card ≤ S.card := Finset.card_le_card hT.1
  omega

end HyperRamsey

import Mathlib

/-! # The Fibonacci–Divisibility Pigeonhole Bridge

A cross-domain result connecting combinatorial pigeonhole arguments with the
number-theoretic divisibility structure of the Fibonacci numbers.

We work with `Nat.fib` (`fib 0 = 0`, `fib 1 = 1`, `fib (n+2) = fib (n+1) + fib n`)
and the *strong divisibility* identity `Nat.fib_gcd`:
`fib (gcd m n) = gcd (fib m) (fib n)`.

## Corrections to the original specification

The original informal specification contained three statements that are literally
false; each has been corrected and the change is documented at the relevant theorem.

* **Theorem 2** was stated with `m ≥ 2`.  This is false: `fib 2 = 1` divides
  `fib 3 = 2`, yet `2 ∤ 3`.  The hypothesis must be `3 ≤ m` (because
  `fib 1 = fib 2 = 1`, the indices `1` and `2` are *not* pinned down by their
  Fibonacci values).  The corrected hypothesis is used here.
* **Theorems 3 and 4** were stated as `∃ i j, i < j ∧ (... ∣ ...)` with a fixed
  divisibility direction.  This is false because the *index* order `i < j` need not
  agree with the *magnitude* order of the values (e.g. `f 0` could be `4` and `f 1`
  could be `2`, giving `f 1 ∣ f 0` but not `f 0 ∣ f 1`).  The correct statement uses
  `i ≠ j`, which is what a pigeonhole argument actually yields.
* **Theorem 5** was stated over indices with `2 ≤ k`; for the *equivalence* to hold
  the lower bound must be `3 ≤ k`, for the same reason as Theorem 2.

The genuine bridge: on indices `≥ 3`, the divisibility poset of Fibonacci numbers is
isomorphic to the divisibility poset of the indices (`fib_dvd_iff`), so a pigeonhole
argument on index divisibility transfers *bidirectionally* to Fibonacci divisibility.
-/

namespace FibPigeonhole

/-! ## Theorem 1 — `fib_dvd_of_dvd` -/

/-- **Theorem 1.** If `m ∣ n` then `fib m ∣ fib n`.

Proof via strong divisibility: since `m ∣ n`, `gcd m n = m`, so
`gcd (fib m) (fib n) = fib (gcd m n) = fib m`, whence `fib m ∣ fib n`. -/
theorem fib_dvd_of_dvd {m n : ℕ} (h : m ∣ n) : Nat.fib m ∣ Nat.fib n := by
  have hg := Nat.fib_gcd m n
  rw [Nat.gcd_eq_left h] at hg
  exact hg ▸ Nat.gcd_dvd_right _ _

/-! ## Theorem 2 — `dvd_of_fib_dvd` (corrected: `3 ≤ m`) -/

/-- **Theorem 2 (corrected).** If `3 ≤ m` and `fib m ∣ fib n`, then `m ∣ n`.

The original hypothesis `2 ≤ m` is false (`fib 2 = 1 ∣ fib 3 = 2` but `2 ∤ 3`).

Proof: `fib m ∣ gcd (fib m) (fib n) = fib (gcd m n)`.  Writing `d = gcd m n`, we have
`d ∣ m` (so `d ≤ m`) and `fib m ∣ fib d`.  Hence `fib m ≤ fib d` while monotonicity
gives `fib d ≤ fib m`, so `fib d = fib m`.  Since `fib` is strictly monotone on
`Set.Ici 2` and `m ≥ 3`, this forces `d = m` (the case `d ≤ 1` is impossible since
`fib m ≥ fib 3 = 2 > 1`), i.e. `m ∣ n`. -/
theorem dvd_of_fib_dvd {m n : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (h : Nat.fib m ∣ Nat.fib n) : m ∣ n := by
  by_contra hmn
  -- `Nat.fib m ∣ Nat.gcd (Nat.fib m) (Nat.fib n)`.
  have h_gcd : Nat.fib m ∣ Nat.gcd (Nat.fib m) (Nat.fib n) := Nat.dvd_gcd dvd_rfl h
  -- By `Nat.fib_gcd`, this gcd is `Nat.fib (Nat.gcd m n)`.
  have h_fib_d : Nat.fib m ∣ Nat.fib (Nat.gcd m n) := by
    rwa [Nat.fib_gcd] at *
  -- Since `m ∤ n`, `gcd m n < m`.
  have h_d_lt_m : Nat.gcd m n < m :=
    lt_of_le_of_ne (Nat.le_of_dvd (by linarith) (Nat.gcd_dvd_left _ _))
      fun con => hmn <| con ▸ Nat.gcd_dvd_right _ _
  by_cases h₂ : Nat.gcd m n < 2
  · interval_cases _ : Nat.gcd m n <;> simp_all +decide
    linarith [Nat.le_fib_add_one m]
  · exact absurd (Nat.le_of_dvd (Nat.fib_pos.mpr (by linarith)) h_fib_d)
      (not_le_of_gt (by rw [Nat.fib_lt_fib] <;> linarith))

/-- **The bridge (poset isomorphism).** For `3 ≤ m`, `fib m ∣ fib n ↔ m ∣ n`.
On indices `≥ 3` the Fibonacci divisibility poset and the index divisibility poset
coincide. -/
theorem fib_dvd_iff {m n : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : Nat.fib m ∣ Nat.fib n ↔ m ∣ n :=
  ⟨dvd_of_fib_dvd hm, fib_dvd_of_dvd⟩

/-! ## Combinatorial helper: equal odd parts give comparability -/

/-- If two numbers have the same odd part (`a / 2 ^ v₂ a`), then one divides the other.
Writing `a = 2^va * o` and `b = 2^vb * o` with `o` the common odd part, the smaller
power of two divides the larger. -/
theorem comparable_of_ordCompl_eq {a b : ℕ}
    (h : a / 2 ^ (a.factorization 2) = b / 2 ^ (b.factorization 2)) :
    a ∣ b ∨ b ∣ a := by
  by_cases h_pow : Nat.factorization a 2 ≤ Nat.factorization b 2
  · exact Or.inl (by
      rw [← Nat.mul_div_cancel' (Nat.ordProj_dvd a 2), ← Nat.mul_div_cancel' (Nat.ordProj_dvd b 2)]
      exact mul_dvd_mul (pow_dvd_pow _ h_pow) (by aesop))
  · have := Nat.div_mul_cancel (Nat.ordProj_dvd a 2)
    have := Nat.div_mul_cancel (Nat.ordProj_dvd b 2)
    simp_all +decide
    exact Or.inr (this ▸ ‹b / 2 ^ b.factorization 2 * 2 ^ a.factorization 2 = a› ▸
      Nat.mul_dvd_mul_left _ (pow_dvd_pow _ h_pow.le))

/-! ## Theorem 3 — `pigeonhole_divisibility` (corrected: `i ≠ j`) -/

exist distinct `i, j` with `(f i).val + 1 ∣ (f j).val + 1`.

The original `i < j` with a fixed divisibility direction is false (index order need
not match magnitude order); the correct conclusion is `i ≠ j`.

Proof: each value `a_i = (f i).val + 1 ∈ {1, …, 2n}` has an odd part in

pair so the divisibility points the right way.

(The hypothesis `1 ≤ n`, requested in the original statement, is kept for faithfulness
but is not needed: for `n = 0` no `f` can take a value in the empty type `Fin 0`.) -/
theorem pigeonhole_divisibility {n : ℕ} (_hn : 1 ≤ n) (f : Fin (n + 1) → Fin (2 * n)) :
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ ((f i : ℕ) + 1) ∣ ((f j : ℕ) + 1) := by
  by_contra h_contra
  -- The odd-part function, valued in the `n` odd numbers `{1, 3, …, 2n-1}`.
  set g : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ := fun i => ((f i).val + 1) / 2 ^ (Nat.factorization ((f i).val + 1) 2)
  have hg : ∀ i, g i ∈ Finset.image (fun k => 2 * k + 1) (Finset.range n) := by
    intro i
    have hg_odd : Odd (g i) :=
      Nat.odd_iff.mpr (Nat.mod_two_ne_zero.mp fun h =>
        absurd (Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero h) (Nat.not_dvd_ordCompl (by norm_num) (by norm_num)))
    have hg_range : g i < 2 * n + 1 :=
      lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.div_le_self _ _) (by linarith [Fin.is_lt (f i)])
    have hg_lt : g i < 2 * n := by grind
    have hg_le : g i ≤ 2 * n - 1 := Nat.le_sub_one_of_lt hg_lt
    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hg_odd
    exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨k, Finset.mem_range.mpr (by linarith), by linarith⟩
  -- Pigeonhole: `n + 1` indices into a set of `n` odd parts gives a repeat.
  obtain ⟨i, j, hij, h_eq⟩ : ∃ i j : Fin (n + 1), i ≠ j ∧ g i = g j := by
    by_cases h_inj : Function.Injective g
    · exact absurd

          Finset.image (fun k => 2 * k + 1) (Finset.range n) from
          Finset.image_subset_iff.mpr fun i _ => hg i))
        (by rw [Finset.card_image_of_injective _ h_inj]
            simp +arith +decide [Finset.card_image_of_injective, Function.Injective])
    · simpa [Function.Injective, and_comm] using h_inj
  -- Equal odd parts make the two values comparable.
  have h_eq_factors : (f i).val + 1 ∣ (f j).val + 1 ∨ (f j).val + 1 ∣ (f i).val + 1 := by
    have h_eq_factors : (f i).val + 1 = 2 ^ (Nat.factorization ((f i).val + 1) 2) * g i ∧

      ⟨Eq.symm (Nat.mul_div_cancel' (Nat.ordProj_dvd _ _)),

    rcases le_total (Nat.factorization (f i + 1) 2) (Nat.factorization (f j + 1) 2) with h | h <;>
